paper.title_en: Floquet dark-mode manipulation in a three-mode optomechanical system
paper.abstract_en: We propose a Floquet sideband method to manipulate the dark-mode effect in a three-mode optomechanical system consisting of a single cavity mode coupled to two mechanical modes. We introduce a periodic frequency modulation for one mechanical mode to generate the Floquet sidebands, one of which is selected to match the resonance frequency of the other mechanical mode, allowing complete destructive interference to produce a mechanical dark mode decoupled from the cavity mode. The semiclassical operating point is determined self-consistently within the framework for linearization of optomechanical interaction, and the linear stability is examined under the rotating-wave approximation. We evaluate the validity of the approximate Hamiltonian by examining the fidelity between the states governed by the approximate and exact Hamiltonians. We further demonstrate dark-mode control by inspecting the bright/dark-mode populations of the system, when a frequency detuning is introduced suddenly. These results may provide a basis for further study of quantum-state storage using the Floquet mechanical dark modes.
